original_question: Let Cl(R^d) be the compact metric space of closed subsets of R^d with the Chabauty-Fell topology. Determine all Borel probability measures on Cl(R^d) that are invariant under the natural action of SL_d(R), and likewise determine all such measures invariant under the natural action of ASL_d(R).
target_in_paper: Problem 2.8.1 (J. Marklof) in Section 2.8.1, "On a Problem of J. Marklof".
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the core of the paper's official problem almost verbatim: it uses the Chabauty-Fell space of closed subsets of R^d, asks for Borel probability measures invariant under the SL_d(R) action, and separately asks for the analogous classification for ASL_d(R).
missing_details: The paper fixes d as an integer with d >= 1.
The action should be made explicit: a group element acts on a closed set by transporting it, i.e. F is sent to its image under the linear or affine map.
SL_d(R) should be identified as the group of determinant-one matrices, equivalently the volume- and orientation-preserving linear transformations of R^d.
ASL_d(R) should be identified as the group of volume- and orientation-preserving affine maps of R^d.
To make the question fully stand-alone, it should be stated as two separate classification problems on the same compact metric space Cl(R^d).
refined_question: Let d >= 1 be a fixed integer, and let Cl(R^d) denote the compact metric space of closed subsets of R^d endowed with the Chabauty-Fell topology. The groups SL_d(R) and ASL_d(R) act on Cl(R^d) by transport of closed sets: for g acting on R^d and F in Cl(R^d), set g.F = {g(x) : x in F}. Classify all Borel probability measures on Cl(R^d) that are invariant under the action of SL_d(R), and separately classify all Borel probability measures on Cl(R^d) that are invariant under the action of ASL_d(R), where SL_d(R) is the group of volume- and orientation-preserving linear transformations of R^d and ASL_d(R) is the group of volume- and orientation-preserving affine maps of R^d.
justification: Section 2.8.1 states exactly this Marklof problem. The surrounding text defines the ambient space Cl(R^d), specifies that it is compact metric in the Chabauty-Fell topology, explains that groups act on it by transporting closed sets, and defines the two acting groups SL_d(R) and ASL_d(R). The only sharpening needed was to make those implicit definitions explicit so that the question is fully stand-alone while remaining no broader than the paper's formal problem statement.
